requirements.text: Config-derived agency policy must be enforced from CodeWiki prompt/system instruction injection, not just skill prose.
Skills must not hard-code task-level stop as the automation boundary; they must defer to .codewiki/config.json agency settings.
Agent continuation must stop at configured stop gates even when config level/cadence permits sprint or roadmap continuation.

evidence_mapping.evidence: User approved SAC-001 and SAC-002 after editing SAC-002 to place primary enforcement in CodeWiki prompt/system instruction injection.
.codewiki/config.json sets codewiki.agency.level=sprint and approval_cadence=sprint with explicit stop_gates.

summary: Accepted config-derived agency enforcement decision: CodeWiki must read .codewiki/config.json and enforce agency continuation/stop behavior through prompt/system instruction injection, with skills aligned to defer to config rather than hard-code one-task stopping.

decision_table.title: Accepted config-derived agency enforcement decision: CodeWiki must read .codewiki/config.json and enforce agency continuation/stop behavior through prompt/system instruction injection, with skills aligned to defer to config rather than hard-code one-task stopping.

rows.question: SAC-001

state_delta.current: The implementation skill says "Execute one self-contained roadmap task at a time" and its output guidance ends at one task, which biases agents to stop after a task even when .codewiki/config.json sets agency.level/approval_cadence to sprint.
state_delta.desired: CodeWiki skills must read .codewiki/config.json and adjust automation/continuation behavior to the configured agency boundary before deciding whether to stop after a task.

rows.proposed_change: Update skills so task execution remains atomic inside a task, but after task-close the agent checks codewiki.agency.level, approval_cadence, budgets, and stop_gates; if configured for sprint/roadmap and no stop gate is active, continue to the next scoped task instead of stopping by default.
rows.rationale: Repo config currently says agency.level=sprint and approval_cadence=sprint, so stopping after TASK-099 was contrary to project policy.

risk.notes: medium: overly broad continuation could run past validation/risk gates unless stop gates remain explicit.

options.label: Keep one-task skill default; rejected by user feedback and config.
Always run whole sprint; too rigid because config must determine agency.

rows.expected_outcome: Agents follow deterministic project config for continuation boundaries and do not hard-code task-level approval cadence.

rows.question: SAC-002

state_delta.current: CodeWiki intercepts agent startup/response context and appends CodeWiki instructions to the system prompt, but the injected instructions and skills do not yet make config-derived agency policy deterministic.
state_delta.desired: The CodeWiki prompt injection/system-contract path should enforce reading .codewiki/config.json and using config-derived agency policy before continuation/stop decisions; skills should not contradict that policy.

rows.proposed_change: Update the CodeWiki prompt/system instruction injection as the primary enforcement point for agency config: read .codewiki/config.json and use codewiki.agency.default_scope, budgets, parallelism, level, approval_cadence, context_reset, and stop_gates to select continuation and stop conditions. Update skills only as supporting guidance so they defer to config rather than hard-code task-level stopping.
rows.rationale: The system-prompt injection path is more reliable than skill prose alone because it is always appended to the agent prompt; skills still need alignment to avoid the wrong one-task pattern.

risk.notes: medium: prompt injection changes affect live agent behavior and require reload after source changes.

options.label: Only update skills; weaker because the system prompt can still omit agency config.
Only update developer prompt; not repo-owned and not deterministic.

rows.expected_outcome: Agents get deterministic config-derived agency instructions from the system prompt injection path, with skills aligned as non-contradictory support.
